description:
src/event.rs:226-245:

    let is_per_user_only = patch_val
        .as_object()
        .map(|m| {
            m.iter()
                .all(|(k, v)| v.is_null() || B::is_per_user_property(k))
        })
        .unwrap_or(false);

This treats a patch entry with value: null as 'matches per-user' for routing purposes. Concretely, an all-null patch like { "title": null, "description": null } evaluates is_per_user_only = true (every value is null) and routes to update_per_user_properties even though the keys are shared properties. update_per_user_properties on the default impl falls back to update_object so this is observably correct, but a backend that overrode update_per_user_properties to scope storage to the user would receive a patch trying to clear shared properties via the per-user code path.

Spec basis: draft-ietf-jmap-calendars-26 §5.4 (line 1300 onward) says the per-user property *list* is keywords/color/freeBusyStatus/useDefaultAlerts/alerts. The spec does not say 'a clear of any property is treated as per-user'. The all-null exemption appears to be an attempt to handle 'set all per-user properties to default' as a no-op but accidentally also matches 'clear shared properties'.

Recommended clarification: only match on key, not on null value. Replace 'v.is_null() || B::is_per_user_property(k)' with just 'B::is_per_user_property(k)'. If the intent was to make a clear-only patch route by shared status, document that explicitly with a comment, but the spec doesn't require that.

Test coverage: the three routing tests in event.rs:1101-1169 all use non-null values, so this edge case is uncovered.

P3 because the default backend impl makes the bug invisible. Higher severity for any backend that actually splits per-user storage.
title: Per-user-property routing logic in event.rs:226-245 handles 'all-null' patch as per-user — consider clarification
